bribeShareOfStake.citation: A bribe as a share of what the favor is worth to the person offering it. Spread 0.05 to 0.2; surveys of firms report bribes of a few percent to over ten percent of contract value (World Bank Enterprise Surveys, bribery incidence and depth).

corruptionTraitWeight.citation: Weight on risk-taking and low reliability (each -2 to 2, scaled to -1 to 1): people high in honesty-humility and conscientiousness are less willing to bribe or be bribed (Ashton and Lee 2008; Hilbig and Zettler 2009, Journal of Research in Personality 43(3):516-519). Spread 0.5 to 2.

corruptionNeedWeight.citation: Weight on money pressure: the bribe against the official's month of living costs, and their own cash against that month. Financial strain raises willingness to accept (Gorodnichenko and Sabirianova Peter 2007, Journal of Public Economics 91(5-6):963-991, on public-sector pay and bribery). Spread 0.5 to 2.

corruptionTieWeight.citation: Weight on closeness between the two: a bribe passes through existing ties (Rose-Ackerman and Palifka 2016, Corruption and Government, ch. 6). Spread 0.5 to 2.

corruptionHonestPull.citation: The pull of not offering or not taking, against which the bribe is weighed. Checked so a corrupt act happens only where traits and circumstances support it. Spread 1.5 to 3.

corruptionTellWeight.citation: Weight on how far the tie between the two parties soured when deciding to tell someone: a partner in a crime who falls out with the other is the classic leak (Rose-Ackerman and Palifka 2016, ch. 9, on whistleblowers and turned witnesses). Spread 2 to 8.

corruptionQuietPull.citation: The pull of keeping quiet about a crime one took part in. Spread 0.5 to 2.

daysPerMonth.citation: A month of daily living costs, rounded to 30 days.
